item.title: Kosovo PM Kurti egged in parliament amid political crisis
item.description: Kosovo has held three elections in over two years. Albin Kurti's ruling Vetevendosje is struggling to garner the two-thirds majority required to elect a president.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: War, terror, diplomacy: What if Israel takes Al-Aqsa Mosque?
item.description: Reports from Jerusalem suggest that Israeli authorities are taking over one of Islam's holiest sites, the Al-Aqsa Mosque. If they do, experts say anything could happen, from war to terrorism to ending diplomatic ties.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Typhoon Dolphin hits Japan as China braces for coming storm
item.description: A typhoon is lashing Japan's south, causing injuries and blackouts. It is now headed for China, where ports have been closed in preparation.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Ceuta: Spain sets up border controls on travelers from Italy
item.description: Spain had warned Italy it would impose entry checks on visitors unless Rome halts its controls by Sunday. Even though they don't share a land border, the countries entered a spat after the Ceuta border rush.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Colombia: Trump ally De la Espriella takes office
item.description: Conservative Abelardo de la Espriella was sworn in as Colombia's president, promising to crack down on armed drug gangs.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Iceland’s EU vote: A nation divided over Europe
item.description: Security concerns, control over fishing rights and rising living costs are shaping Iceland's debate over whether to restart talks on joining the European Union.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Migrant tunnels in Lithuania direct suspicion towards Minsk
item.description: Lithuania's border guards have discovered tunnels through which migrants are trying to enter the country from Belarus. Analysts see them as a means to destabilize the country.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy makes first visit to Russia-friendly Serbia
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy is making his first visit to Serbia. His host, President Aleksandar Vucic, hopes to score points with the EU, while Zelenskyy seeks more arms from a country that remains friendly to Russia.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: How viable is the potential Iran-Oman Hormuz shipping deal?
item.description: Iran says a shipping accord with Oman is in its final stages, but analysts warn sanctions, security concerns and rival US-Iran goals could limit its impact.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing seeks legitimacy in Thailand
item.description: Bangkok rolled out the red carpet for the Myanmar leader, but experts say the former junta chief still faces major obstacles in his bid for regional acceptance.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ebola: Africa CDC plans to use vaccine for different strain as outbreak spreads
item.description: The head of the Africa Centres for Disease Control pledged to deploy a vaccine for a previous Ebola strain in the current DRC outbreak, with test cases indicating a potentially lifesaving level of protection.
